seats.name: Mark Cuban
seats.question: Why does this win, and what stops a bigger player from crushing it?
seats.style: Straight equity, sometimes larger checks for control; walks instantly on bad math or a founder who dodges
seats.tells: Founder cannot state numbers from memory; product is a feature not a company; licensing fantasies

seats.name: Kevin O'Leary
seats.pillar: Money, valuation, and return on capital
seats.question: How and when do I get my money back, and what is this actually worth?
seats.style: Royalty deals (per unit or % until repaid, then drops), venture debt, low equity plus royalty; loves recurring revenue
seats.tells: Crazy valuation, no path to repayment, founder in love with product not profit

seats.name: Lori Greiner
seats.pillar: Consumer product, retail, and TV/QVC sellability
seats.question: Is this a hero or a zero on the shelf, and can I sell it at scale through retail and TV?
seats.style: Equity for retail/QVC distribution, sometimes with a loan component; moves fast on products she can demo
seats.tells: Not a physical product she can sell; no patent or protection; weak margins at wholesale

seats.name: Barbara Corcoran
seats.pillar: The founder, sales grit, and gut read
seats.question: Would I bet on this person, and can they sell their way through the hard parts?
seats.style: Equity bets on the person; conditional offers tied to founder behaviour (full-time, hire a partner, fix one thing)
seats.tells: Excuses, blaming the market, founders who talk over each other, no hunger

seats.name: Daymond John
seats.question: Is this a brand people will wear and pay for, and can we make it cheaply at scale?
seats.dimension: Brand strength and cost to produce
seats.style: Equity plus licensing/manufacturing help; sometimes higher equity in exchange for sourcing and distribution
seats.tells: No brand story, manufacturing not figured out, founders who have not sold anything themselves

seats.name: Robert Herjavec
seats.pillar: B2B, software, security, and sales process
seats.question: How do you sell this to businesses repeatably, and what does the pipeline look like?
seats.style: Straight equity; likes founders who have sold enterprise deals themselves
seats.tells: No sales process, no pipeline numbers, founder who has never cold-called

seats.name: Aman Gupta
seats.pillar: D2C brand building and marketing in India
seats.question: Can this become a loved consumer brand in India, and is the marketing engine real?
seats.style: Equity, often with marketing/brand support; likes co-investing with another Shark
seats.tells: No brand differentiation, founders who want to outsource marketing, premium pricing without proof

seats.name: Namita Thapar
seats.question: Are the unit economics and the governance sound enough that this survives scrutiny?
seats.style: Equity with conditions on governance and reporting; out fast on sectors outside her expertise
seats.tells: Fuzzy numbers, regulatory risk not addressed, founders who undervalue process

seats.name: Anupam Mittal
seats.pillar: Internet marketplaces, consumer tech, and network effects
seats.question: Where is the network effect or the lock-in, and how big can this get online?
seats.style: Equity; pushes back hard on valuation, then negotiates toward a middle
seats.tells: Copycat idea, no retention data, founder ignores the bigger platform risk

seats.name: Vineeta Singh
seats.pillar: D2C execution, customer obsession, and scaling a consumer brand
seats.question: Does the customer love this, and can the founder execute the next 10x?
seats.style: Equity, often with hands-on operating help; conditional on metrics (repeat rate, CAC)
seats.tells: Low repeat purchase, no customer insight, founders who have not spoken to customers

seats.name: Peyush Bansal
seats.question: What problem does this solve, how well, and can the operations deliver it every day?
seats.style: Equity; likes to mentor; sometimes offers more money for more equity to go deep
seats.tells: Solution looking for a problem, founder cannot explain the ops, vanity metrics
